newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down 2.0 pct on property worries.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down 2.0 pct on property worries.

text.p: Thai stocks extended losses for the fifth straight day on Wednesday as investors sold stocks in key sectors amid worries some cash-strapped property firms may be unable to repay loans, brokers said.
The SET index moved in the negative zone throughout the session and finished 2.0 percent lower at 906.11 or down 18.45 points on 3.7 billion baht trade.

"Investors continued to sell property, finance and bank issues today on worries that property firms with cashflow problems may not be able to pay off debts," said Thaneit Khantigaroon of Ekachart Finance and Securities.

Brokers said investors sold finance and bank stocks as they feared that some of these financial institutions may face similar cashflow problems if they were hit by loan defaults from clients in the property sector.

Investors remained worried about cashflow problems in the property sector after police on Tuesday issued a warrant for the arrest of the head of suspended property firm Somprasong Group Plc, on charges of falsifying the company's financial statements.
"Investors hesitated to invest today and also awaited key economic indicators from the central bank," Thaneit said.
